title: Horsepower Variants: Mechanical, Metric, Electrical, Boiler
h1: Horsepower variants — mechanical, metric, electrical, boiler
description: 1 hp (mechanical) = 745.7 W. 1 PS = 735.5 W. 1 electrical hp = 746 W. 1 boiler hp = 9810 W. Four horsepowers, four numbers.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Horsepower is not one unit. Four common variants differ by 1–1300%.
body: The horsepower is a family of units, not a single one. Each variant traces back to a different historical definition — Watt's mechanical hp, continental Europe's metric hp, the electrical industry's rounded value, and the boiler industry's steam-based hp.

> Mechanical hp (US, imperial): 745.6999 W
> Metric hp / PS / CV: 735.4988 W (1.4% smaller)
> Electrical hp: 746 W (rounded, motor nameplate standard)
> Boiler hp: 9809.5 W (evaporation of 34.5 lb water/hr at 212 °F)
Mechanical: US automotive, US pump specs. Metric (PS/CV): European cars, motorcycles. Electrical: US and international motor nameplates. Boiler: steam boiler ratings, industrial heating.
## Worked example — European vs US car spec
'300 PS turbo' = 220.65 kW = 295.9 hp mechanical. US press quotes 300 hp — same car, 4 hp discrepancy. On boutique high-output cars, this compounds through engine mods and warranty limits.
hp without a qualifier is ambiguous. Mechanical vs metric differs by 1.4%; boiler is a completely different scale.

faqs.a: Only for mechanical hp. Metric hp defined as 75 kgf·m/s = 735.5 W.

faqs.q: Which one does a motor nameplate use?
faqs.a: Electrical hp (746 W) — a convenient rounded value for AC motor ratings.
